blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is known for its majestic Baobab trees. These can grow to an enormous size and have a unique shape. The Park is also famous as it has the largest concentration of elephants in the world! You can see herds of up to 300 elephants around the Tarangire River. The River is the primary source of fresh water for the animals. In the dry season, they come here to drink or just to enjoy a bath to cool off from the hot sun. During the end of dry season, elephants dig into the riverbed to reveal underground water, or are looking for Baobab trees to slake their thirst.
blocks.html: The majestic Baobab trees are what Tarangire National Park is best known for. They can reach an enormous size and take on a shape all of their own. The park is also renowned for having the largest concentration of elephants in the world: around the Tarangire River you can come across herds of up to 300 of them. For the animals, this river is the main supply of fresh water. In the dry season they gather here to drink, or simply to bathe and cool down from the heat of the sun. Towards the end of the dry season the elephants dig into the riverbed to uncover water below the surface, or they search out Baobab trees to quench their thirst.

blocks.orig: Apart from elephants, Tarangire is a paradise for bird lovers. From parrots, hornbills, lovebirds and lilac breasted rollers to Kori bustards, eagles and vultures. The swamps in Tarangire National Park have one of the largest number of breeding bird species in the world. In the area around these swamps you can also see lions, leopards, cheetahs and even tree-climbing pythons.
blocks.html: Elephants aside, bird lovers will find Tarangire a paradise, with everything from parrots, hornbills, lovebirds and lilac breasted rollers to Kori bustards, eagles and vultures. The number of breeding bird species in the swamps of Tarangire National Park is among the largest in the world. Around these swamps you can also spot lions, leopards, cheetahs and even pythons that climb trees.

blocks.orig: Tarangire is one of the lesser known parks in Tanzania, but it still has an authentic safari atmosphere. The hilly landscape scattered with huge Baobab trees against the blue sky is breathtaking.
blocks.html: Although Tarangire is one of Tanzania's less familiar parks, the safari atmosphere here still feels authentic. Rolling hills dotted with huge Baobab trees under a blue sky make for a breathtaking landscape.

blocks.orig: Travel tip from our experts about Tarangire National Park
blocks.html: Our experts' travel tip for Tarangire National Park

blocks.orig: My name is Mark, and I have been a guide for 15 years at Tarangire National Park. Our guests love Tarangire mainly due to the abundance of elephants and huge Baobab trees. Tarangire is fairly huge and there is a lot to see. I would recommend spending one day in the north and one day in the remote south of the park
blocks.html: I'm Mark, and I have spent 15 years guiding at Tarangire National Park. What our guests love most about Tarangire is the abundance of elephants and the huge Baobab trees. The park is fairly large and has plenty to see, so my advice is to spend one day in the north and another in the remote south of the park

blocks.orig: Tarangire is a great year round park for game viewing. Especially during the dry season (June – October) when animals gather around the main water source in the area, the Tarangire River. Lots of animals migrate out of the park during the rainy season (April-May) due to the black cotton soil that’s bad for their hoofs.
blocks.html: Tarangire offers great game viewing all year round. This is especially true in the dry season (June – October), when the animals gather around the area's main water source, the Tarangire River. During the rainy season (April-May) many animals move out of the park, because the black cotton soil is bad for their hoofs.

blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park has the largest concentrations of elephants in the world, giant Baobab trees, beautiful landscapes, lions, leopards, cheetahs, monkeys, and it’s a true paradise for bird lovers.
blocks.html: In Tarangire National Park you will find the largest concentrations of elephants in the world, giant Baobab trees, beautiful scenery, lions, leopards, cheetahs and monkeys, and for bird lovers it is a true paradise.
